3. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Vikas seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 14 of 2022, under Sections 376 I.P.C. and 5(j)(ii), 5(i), 6 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act), P.S. entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The F.I.R. of the matter was lodged on 11.1.2022, under Sections 376 I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act,
2012 by Nandu against the applicant alleging therein that his daughter aged about 17 years used to talk with the applicant for about two years.
The applicant on false promise to marry, established physical relationship with her due to which she became pregnant.

When she told him to marry her,
he refused.
His parents also refused for marriage.
His daughter is having pregnancy of about three months.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the victim and the applicant were in love with each other since last two years and there was physical relationship between them since then.

It is argued that as per disclosure in the charge sheet after the victim delivered a child DNA examination would be done,
but till date no DNA examination has been conducted.
It is argued that in the records of the hospital where the victim was admitted, her age has been mentioned as 21 years and as such she is a major girl.
It is argued that even the medical examination of the victim was done in which her age was stated to be 17 years by the doctor.
It is argued that implication of the applicant in the present case is false as the victim was a consenting party.
It is argued that the applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para- 18 of the affidavit and is in jail since 14.1.2022.

6. Per contra, learned State counsel and learned counsel fro the first informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that as per the School Certificate of Class-8th, the date of birth of the victim was recorded therein as 04.08.2007 and as such she was aged about 14 years at the time of incident.
It is argued that since the victim was a minor her consent cannot be looked into.
It is argued that the applicant is named in the F.I.R., the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. and there are allegations against him.
It is argued that charge sheet in the matter has been submitted against the applicant.
It is argued that bail application of the applicant be rejected.

7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that as of now only document with regards to age of the victim is School Leaving Certificate of Class-8th.
Perusal of the same would go to show that the victim was aged about 14 years at the time of incident and as such she was a minor and consent of a minor is of no worth.
8. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 18.9.2023 Naresh  Vikas vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185300876/
